reason: Production startup can create callable ASGI/WSGI handlers with development signing-key defaults when variables are omitted, because production checks are deployment-only (settings.py:10,117; checks.py:61; asgi.py:7; Dockerfile:16). This is a reproduced release guard gap, but the claimed deployed auth bypass depends on unverified live key and ingress configuration. The private runbook requires checks. Retain as a release blocker, not a confirmed production compromise.

Existing 24-hour subject/expiry-only bearer tokens remain accepted after a password change and stop when the account is disabled (tokens.py:11,18-47; authentication.py:22-32). The claim of violating a promised revocation boundary was not supported: browser sign-out explicitly discards local memory only, no reset/revoke API is promised, and no independent token-acquisition vulnerability was found. Retain the recovery limitation as hardening.
